description: Scored company briefs from SEC EDGAR for 14 large US companies (Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Amazon, Walmart, JPMorgan, Bank of America, Exxon, Pfizer, Lilly, J&J, UnitedHealth, Netflix, Disney): fundamentals, filing risk (8-K items, 13D, Form 4), insider activity, balance sheet strength, a peer ranking, earnings quality, shareholder returns (buybacks and dividends), interest coverage, the investment cycle (capex), settlement fails (SEC fails-to-deliver) and institutional ownership (13F). Every input carries its SEC citation. POST /v1/brief {vertical, entity_id} returns one scored brief; POST /v1/overview returns every brief at once; POST /v1/verticals lists them. Verticals: fundamentals, filing-risk, insider-activity, balance-sheet, peer-ranking, public-attention, earnings-quality, shareholder-returns, interest-coverage, investment-cycle, settlement-fails, institutional-ownership. Raw scored series: /v1/signals, /v1/signal, /v1/explain, /v1/catalog, /v1/events. POST /v1/evidence-packet {entity_id, from?, to?, kinds?, q?}: every dated, cited regulatory event for one entity in up to 366 days, with per-source coverage and hashes. Briefs carry signed input attestations (Ed25519) that never change a score. Every response is a single JSON object. Research signal, not investment advice.

rpc_types.notes: POST /v1/verticals, POST /v1/brief, POST /v1/overview, POST /v1/signals, POST /v1/signal, POST /v1/explain, POST /v1/catalog, POST /v1/events, POST /v1/evidence-packet; GET /v1/version, /v1/health. JSON body only. Bad input returns 400 + JSON.

serving.backend: Node.js HTTP server (zero npm dependencies) behind a RelayMiner at http://<container>:8080. No caller auth. Answers come from a private hub refreshed by a scheduled collector of official public data; 5-minute cache.
serving.notes: Gateway operators: configure as type passthrough with rpc_types ["rest"].
